claims.text: Conventional single-phase ZrB2 requires sintering temperatures above 2300 °C.
Conventionally sintered single-phase ZrB2 has significant porosity.
Conventionally sintered single-phase ZrB2 has compromised mechanical strength.
SPS can produce single-phase ZrB2 at approximately 2000 °C.
SPS is a viable method for preparing sintered bulk materials.
Real-time thermometry and dilatometry can optimize SPS pulse duration, current density, and heating rate for ZrB2 densification.
Varying material-processing conditions can be used to seek improved densification during SPS.
Short high-temperature exposure during SPS reduces grain coarsening in ZrB2.
Short high-temperature exposure during SPS minimizes pore formation in ZrB2.
Rapid, field-assisted sintering reduces pore nucleation and growth by limiting high-temperature exposure.
In situ monitoring can preserve single-phase ZrB2 by enabling precise adjustment of sintering parameters.
Reduced porosity and improved densification increase the mechanical integrity of SPS-processed ZrB2.
Improved mechanical integrity makes ZrB2 more resistant to chemical degradation in a liquid plating bath.
ZrB2 processed by SPS at approximately 2000 °C will have lower porosity than ZrB2 conventionally sintered above 2300 °C.
SPS-processed ZrB2 will have superior mechanical properties compared with conventionally sintered ZrB2.
SPS-processed ZrB2 will form fewer holes and experience less component failure during more than 1000 hours of liquid plating bath exposure.
Conventionally sintered ZrB2 degrades during long-duration exposure to a liquid plating bath.
The proposed service boundary is more than 1000 hours of liquid plating bath exposure at a controlled moderate temperature.
